authors: Michael Manville, Brian D. Taylor, Evelyn Blumenberg, & Andrew Schouten
title: Vehicle access and falling transit ridership: evidence from Southern California
notes: LA Metro riders are almost 4 times as likely as LA County residents to come from households with incomes under $15,000 per year (44% vs 12%). Proves transit dependency in LA is heavily concentrated in extremely low-income households.

authors: Evelyn Blumenberg, Julene Paul, Miriam Pinski, & Madeline Brozen
title: Transportation and Quality-of-Life Effects of Los Angeles's Mobility Wallet
publication: Journal of the American Planning Association (JAPA), 2026
notes: Evaluates the South LA Universal Basic Mobility pilot. Combined housing and transportation expenditure burden for bottom income quintile households in LA reaches 56%. Flexible mobility subsidies reduced travel time constraints.

authors: Julene Paul, Miriam Pinski, Madeline Brozen, & Evelyn Blumenberg
title: Can Subsidized Carshare Programs Enhance Access for Low-Income Travelers?: BlueLA in Los Angeles
publication: Journal of Planning Education and Research (JPER), Vol. 43, 2023
notes: Low-income transit riders in LA spend disproportionately more time traveling per mile compared to higher-income commuters. Subsidized carshare filled critical transit gaps for non-work trips in Westlake and Pico-Union.

authors: Evelyn Blumenberg, Fariba Siddiq, Samuel Speroni, & Jacob Wasserman
title: Putting automobile debt on the map: Race and the geography of automobile debt in California
publication: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice, Vol. 188, 2024
notes: Automobile debt distress is geographically concentrated in low-income Black and Latino census tracts in LA County where public transit alternatives fail to offer competitive travel times compared to driving.

authors: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LA Metro)
title: NextGen Bus Plan & Equity Focus Communities Framework
publication: LA Metro Board Reports & Equity Hub, 2020
notes: LA Metro defines Equity Focus Communities (EFCs) using median income under $75k, BIPOC density, and zero-vehicle ownership. Shows over 80% of bus riders earned under $20,000 annually prior to NextGen overhaul.

title: L.A. transit riders face scorching heat and lack of shade at bus stops
notes: Fewer than 25% of LA bus stops have shade structures, disproportionately impacting bus riders in low-income South L.A. and Eastside neighborhoods compared to affluent suburbs.

title: Means of Transportation to Work by Household Income (Table B08121) - Los Angeles County
notes: Primary census demographic dataset. Shows households earning under $25k represent over 52% of total bus commuters in LA County, while zero-vehicle household rates exceed 28% in Westlake census tracts.

title: Advance Transit app gives real-time updates on buses
notes: Database entry cited on Slide 9 of class template. Demonstrates how real-time GPS tracking mobile apps reduce wait-time uncertainty for transit-dependent bus riders.
